FINAL IVX OWNED AI PLATFORM
REMOVE RORK FROM THE DEVELOPMENT PATH AND MAKE IVX IA FULLY OWNER-CONTROLLED

EXECUTE END TO END — DO NOT RETURN ONLY A PLAN
DO NOT CLAIM INDEPENDENCE UNTIL IVX CAN OPERATE, CODE, TEST, COMMIT, DEPLOY, MONITOR, AND RECOVER WITHOUT RORK

==================================================
OBJECTIVE
==================================================

Build and deploy IVX IA as an owner-controlled AI engineering platform.

The final system must allow the owner to use IVX IA from:

- IVX mobile app
- IVX web chat
- IVX owner dashboard
- documented IVX API

The normal coding path must not require:

- Rork UI
- Rork sandbox
- Rork agent
- Rork SDK
- Rork API
- Rork deployment hook
- Rork repository proxy
- Rork-owned infrastructure

Rork may assist with this final migration, but after completion IVX IA must run independently.

==================================================
PHASE 1 — OWNER-CONTROLLED ARCHITECTURE
==================================================

Implement this production flow:

IVX Mobile/Web Chat
→ IVX API Gateway
→ IVX Intent Router
→ IVX Persistent Job Queue
→ IVX AI Orchestrator
→ IVX Autonomous Coder
→ Isolated Workspace
→ Owner GitHub
→ Tests and QA
→ Owner Approval
→ Owner Render/EAS/AWS
→ Production Verification
→ IVX Proof Ledger

Every component must be owned by the IVX owner.

For each component document:

- service name
- repository
- runtime
- account owner
- billing owner
- credential variable
- deployment target
- backup method
- monitoring
- Rork dependency

==================================================
PHASE 2 — CREATE THE IVX AI ORCHESTRATOR
==================================================

Create a dedicated owner-controlled service:

ivx-ai-orchestrator

Responsibilities:

- accept owner tasks
- classify intent
- create persistent jobs
- select the correct AI worker
- enforce permissions
- manage retries
- manage checkpoints
- manage owner approvals
- record evidence
- update IVX Chat and dashboards
- monitor job health
- trigger rollback when required

Required job modes:

READ_ONLY
CODE_CHANGE
QA_ONLY
BUILD
DEPLOY
FACTORY
INCIDENT_RESPONSE

==================================================
PHASE 3 — OWNER-CONTROLLED MODEL PROVIDERS
==================================================

Connect IVX IA directly to owner-controlled model credentials.

Support at least:

PRIMARY_CODING_MODEL
SECONDARY_CODING_MODEL
REASONING_MODEL
FAST_ROUTING_MODEL

For every provider document:

- provider
- model
- credential variable
- rate limits
- cost limits
- timeout
- retry policy
- fallback order
- data-retention setting
- availability status

Do not expose secret values.

Do not route through a Rork-owned AI gateway.

==================================================
PHASE 4 — PERSISTENT JOB SYSTEM
==================================================

Create or verify production tables:

ivx_ai_jobs
ivx_ai_job_events
ivx_ai_job_steps
ivx_ai_job_artifacts
ivx_ai_job_approvals
ivx_ai_job_logs
ivx_ai_job_costs
ivx_ai_worker_leases
ivx_ai_checkpoints
ivx_ai_proof_ledger

Each job must store:

- task ID
- owner ID
- conversation ID
- message ID
- original prompt
- normalized goal
- mode
- priority
- status
- stage
- progress
- worker ID
- model provider
- model request ID
- workspace ID
- repository
- branch
- starting SHA
- files inspected
- files changed
- patch checksum
- tests
- typecheck
- lint
- commit SHA
- deployment ID
- build ID
- proof artifacts
- cost
- created time
- started time
- heartbeat
- completed time
- error code
- blocker

Jobs must survive:

- API restart
- worker restart
- Render restart
- mobile restart
- browser refresh
- temporary network loss

==================================================
PHASE 5 — OWNER-CONTROLLED WORKER RUNTIME
==================================================

Move the autonomous worker out of the Rork sandbox.

Deploy it to one owner-controlled environment:

- Render worker service
- AWS ECS/Fargate
- AWS EC2
- Kubernetes
- another approved IVX-owned runtime

Required worker capabilities:

- clone owner repository
- create isolated branch/worktree
- inspect files
- generate patches
- modify files
- run shell commands
- install dependencies
- run tests
- typecheck
- lint
- build
- create commits
- push through owner GitHub API
- inspect logs
- call deployment APIs
- verify production

The worker must use task-scoped credentials and isolated workspaces.

==================================================
PHASE 6 — AUTONOMOUS CODING LOOP
==================================================

Implement the real engineering loop:

INSPECT
→ PLAN
→ PATCH
→ APPLY
→ TEST
→ ANALYZE
→ REVISE
→ TYPECHECK
→ REGRESSION
→ COMMIT
→ AWAIT_OWNER_APPROVAL
→ DEPLOY
→ VERIFY
→ COMPLETE

Set bounded limits:

- maximum model calls
- maximum repair iterations
- maximum runtime
- maximum test duration
- maximum deployment attempts
- maximum cost per job

If a limit is reached:

STATUS: BLOCKED
ERROR CODE: LIMIT_REACHED
return exact evidence.

==================================================
PHASE 7 — ISOLATED ENGINEERING WORKSPACES
==================================================

Every code-change job must receive:

- unique workspace ID
- isolated container or worktree
- repository lock
- clean starting state
- recorded starting SHA
- path restrictions
- command allowlist
- resource limits
- cleanup after completion
- preserved failure artifacts when blocked

No task may edit production files directly.

No two workers may modify the same branch simultaneously.

==================================================
PHASE 8 — OWNER APPROVAL CONTROLS
==================================================

Allow IVX IA to perform automatically:

- inspect code
- inspect logs
- generate plan
- create patch
- run tests
- run typecheck
- run lint
- create isolated commit
- prepare build
- prepare deployment

Require owner approval before:

- push to protected production branch
- production deployment
- database migration affecting production
- destructive data changes
- DNS changes
- credential changes
- payment configuration changes
- infrastructure deletion
- risky rollback

Approval phrases must be task-specific and single-use.

==================================================
PHASE 9 — GITHUB OWNERSHIP
==================================================

Verify:

- canonical IVX repository is owner-controlled
- IVX AI GitHub App or token is owner-controlled
- commits identify IVX AI clearly
- branch protections remain enabled
- Rork collaborators/apps/deploy keys are removed
- IVX worker can create branches and commits
- owner can review and revert every change

Required normal path:

IVX Worker
→ owner GitHub API
→ owner repository
→ owner CI

No Rork repository proxy.

==================================================
PHASE 10 — BUILD AND DEPLOYMENT OWNERSHIP
==================================================

Create owner-controlled build paths for:

BACKEND
- GitHub Actions or Render build
- owner-controlled service

ANDROID
- EAS Build or GitHub Actions
- APK
- AAB
- owner-controlled signing

IOS
- EAS or Apple build pipeline
- owner-controlled bundle ID
- owner-controlled signing
- TestFlight

WEB
- owner-controlled web deployment

No normal build may depend on the Rork sandbox.

==================================================
PHASE 11 — IVX CHAT SYNC
==================================================

All execution requests from IVX IA Chat must create real jobs.

Developer intents:

- fix
- build
- implement
- refactor
- create module
- create app
- test and fix
- deploy
- audit and repair
- senior developer
- autonomous coder

Immediate response:

HTTP 202

{
  "taskId": "...",
  "status": "QUEUED",
  "mode": "...",
  "statusUrl": "...",
  "createdAt": "..."
}

The chat must display real stored events.

No narrative-only fallback for execution requests.

==================================================
PHASE 12 — IVX OWNER DASHBOARD
==================================================

Create an owner-only AI Operations dashboard showing:

- active jobs
- queued jobs
- workers
- current stages
- model providers
- costs
- files changed
- tests
- commits
- builds
- deployments
- approvals
- blockers
- incidents
- rollback status
- job history
- proof ledger

Add controls:

- pause
- resume
- cancel
- retry
- approve
- reject
- rollback
- open logs
- open diff
- open commit
- open deployment

==================================================
PHASE 13 — OBSERVABILITY
==================================================

Implement:

- worker heartbeat monitoring
- API latency
- job duration
- queue depth
- model latency
- model error rate
- test failure rate
- build failure rate
- deployment failure rate
- rollback events
- cost tracking
- crash reporting
- structured trace IDs
- security alerts

Every task must be traceable from chat message to production deployment.

==================================================
PHASE 14 — SECURITY
==================================================

Verify:

- owner authentication
- server-side role checks
- task ownership
- repository restrictions
- secret redaction
- command allowlist
- isolated workspace
- no credential logging
- no direct balance or financial-data modification
- no unauthorized deployment
- no cross-project access
- audit log immutability

Run a security test against all owner-only routes.

==================================================
PHASE 15 — REMOVE RORK FROM THE NORMAL PATH
==================================================

Remove or disable:

- Rork SDKs
- Rork runtime imports
- Rork URLs
- Rork model gateway
- Rork worker calls
- Rork queue
- Rork deployment hooks
- Rork repository router
- Rork Expo project references
- Rork build identifiers
- Rork collaborators and apps
- Rork webhooks
- Rork environment variables

Keep only historical documentation or security blocklists when clearly non-executable.

==================================================
PHASE 16 — LIVE INDEPENDENCE TEST
==================================================

Run this entire test without opening or using Rork:

1. Submit a code-change request from IVX IA Chat.
2. Create one persistent job.
3. Worker claims the job.
4. Owner-controlled model generates a patch.
5. Worker applies the patch.
6. Tests run.
7. Typecheck runs.
8. Commit is created.
9. Owner approves deployment.
10. Owner-controlled deployment runs.
11. Production verification passes.
12. Evidence appears in IVX Chat.
13. Restart the worker.
14. Confirm the job history remains available.
15. Confirm no Rork service was contacted.

Required proof:

- task ID
- worker ID
- model provider
- model request ID
- repository
- starting SHA
- diff
- files changed
- test results
- typecheck
- commit SHA
- approval event
- deployment ID
- runtime commit
- production screenshot
- network-domain list

==================================================
PHASE 17 — APP FACTORY INDEPENDENCE TEST
==================================================

Using only IVX-owned infrastructure, create a small independent pilot app.

APPLICATION:
IVX Investor Tracker

Required:

- new owner GitHub repository
- Expo TypeScript app
- owner login
- investor list
- create/edit investor
- pipeline stage
- notes
- Supabase schema or isolated database
- RLS
- tests
- APK
- backend deployment
- production verification

No Rork agent may author the application code.

No Rork build or deployment path may be used.

==================================================
PHASE 18 — DISASTER RECOVERY
==================================================

Prove IVX IA can recover independently.

Run:

- clean repository clone
- restore job database backup
- restore secrets configuration
- start API
- start worker
- submit test task
- create patch
- run tests
- commit
- deploy to recovery target
- verify production

Record recovery time and blockers.

==================================================
PHASE 19 — FINAL EVIDENCE
==================================================

Return:

OWNER CONTROL
- GitHub
- Render
- Supabase
- AWS
- Expo/EAS
- Apple
- Google Play
- DNS
- AI providers
- worker runtime
- job queue

RORK REMOVAL
- packages removed
- URLs removed
- integrations removed
- access removed
- remaining references
- reason for each retained reference

LIVE CODING PROOF
- task ID
- patch
- tests
- commit
- deployment
- production verification

APP FACTORY PROOF
- repository
- files created
- database
- tests
- APK
- deployment

NETWORK PROOF
- all external domains contacted
- Rork requests: 0

RECOVERY PROOF
- restore test
- recovery duration
- result

==================================================
FINAL ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
==================================================

Do not mark complete until:

[ ] IVX AI orchestrator is owner-controlled.
[ ] Model credentials are owner-controlled.
[ ] Worker runtime is owner-controlled.
[ ] Job queue is owner-controlled.
[ ] GitHub is owner-controlled.
[ ] Builds are owner-controlled.
[ ] Deployments are owner-controlled.
[ ] IVX Chat creates real jobs.
[ ] IVX Dashboard controls jobs.
[ ] Live code-change test passes without Rork.
[ ] Live deployment test passes without Rork.
[ ] App Factory pilot succeeds without Rork.
[ ] Network logs show zero Rork requests.
[ ] Rork access is removed from all production accounts.
[ ] Disaster recovery passes.
[ ] Owner can continue coding without opening Rork.

==================================================

==================================================

Do not return another architecture-only report.
Build, deploy, test, and prove the owner-controlled IVX IA platform now.
